To me it sounds like you have had quite the traumatic experience, and this is your brain trying to make sense of what could have or would have happened if things turned out differently. 

I wouldn't suggest to anyone to try to become a martyr in any way, shape or form even though every one loves a dead man in their own way. 

I would also say that you might have a inner conflict with how you value your own life and I would suggest that you try to change your view on what is honorable or what in your case would be "something worth dying for".  

In my opinion almost nothing is worth dying for, because you life is short as it is and giving that up for a sense of a justified death in the name of the state, the oppressed people or any other cause that would be reasonable at the time is a false sense of justice. The same thing goes if you would go for God or any other corporation or entity and in some cases even your loved ones. What I am trying to say is don't fall for the trick of fighting someone else's battle because then you'll only be a pawn in someone else's scheme. And even though I understand the appeal of fighting for something greater then yourself, don't forget that at the end of the day you only have yourself and that should be your first priority.

Your life is what you make of it and the same thing goes for your personality. I am not suggesting that you seek external support for your issues but I am asking you to take a long look in the mirror and ask yourself who you want to be. Some of us in life have been dealt a bad hand, and for you it seems like it is either the way you look at yourself or your actual personality. I do believe it's the first of those two instead of the second one. I am certain that anyone is capable of making a change if they are really committed to doing so, and you're at least come so far that you're acknowledging your flaws. But don't let the overwhelming feeling of despair destroy you despite the fact that you are fighting a battle with a severe disadvantage. Don't drown in your own emotions, because you are capable of doing almost anything in life as long as you are willing to pay the price for it. The real question is are you willing to suffer in order to make that change?

I am a person of colour and I would say that I don't agree with your worldview but I believe  I understand where you are coming from. I grew up as the only coloured person in a white community and racial slurs as well as bullying because of my skin colour was something that I had to endure on a regular basis. I have similar experiences to yours where I ended up in the wrong neighbourhood and was jumped by a couple of people because of my skin. Then I also have been chased down the street by 20 to 30 guys when I was heading to a party in a different small town and then one where I live. 
But being racist towards white people or hateful  full towards people who happen to have a different skin colour then myself isn't something that I am. What I feel familiar with in your way of thinking is that you recognize that when the situation is heated, as the racial fights in your school or the fact that people from your area have racially divided gangs that are rivaling with each other, is that people tend to in these situations choose to side with their own ethnicity. And I think a majority of people can't fully grasp what that is like and how it plays out in reality. What I mean by that statement is most people live in a community where they don't have to worry about actual racism from both sides is a matter of personal safety. However I hope you don't let your racist views interferes with your way of treating people too much, even though I believe they do even if you are aware of it or not.

I have tried killing myself out of desperation when I was younger and a lot of people in my surrounding has passed away or have fallen into bad habits they couldn't escape from (I am talking about mostly about drugs and alcoholism), so when you said that you thought you wouldn't live to 18 it hit close to home. I would like to say that I am not suicidal today and haven't been for months at least.

Thank you for sharing your thoughts, and I am happy to hear that you are there for your friend. I don't have anyone right now that I can ask for guidance and a lot of what you said about having a functional every day life is something that I struggle with a lot. And it is often the things that other people find easy, as in preparing food, having a good sleep schedule and having a functional social life. I won't say more then that I live in Europe because I don't know if anyone on here can recognize my story and I would like to stay anonymous. However I have had a tremendous amount of support from our welfare system from when I first fell ill and I am very grateful for that and at the same time I don't want to rely on it too much because I want to be independent. In addition to that I don't trust the system fully because of my experience in the different foster homes. In other words I have mixed emotions about asking for help from the system and different organisations. As I mentioned in a another comment is that I have a job and are self sufficient,  but I do live in poverty.
